item.text:
**3B.2 Research Note: Olaf Scholz in 2024**

**Bottom line:** I found strong evidence that Scholz generally **prevented and punished** abusive or extremist conduct inside state/security structures in 2024. I did **not** find reliable evidence that he tolerated police, military, intelligence, prison, militia, or loyalist abuse. The main counterweight is that Germany’s intelligence-surveillance regime was still partly unconstitutional in late 2024, which shows an unresolved abuse-risk in the system, but not clear personal tolerance by Scholz.

| Evidence | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---|
| **“Bundeskanzler Scholz zur aktuellen Sicherheitslage: Terror sagen wir den Kampf an”** - Deutscher Bundestag - **6 Jun 2024** - https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2024/kw23-de-regierungserklaerung-1006098 | Scholz responded to the Mannheim police killing by backing tougher punishment, saying attackers must face “the full force of the law,” that there is no “rule of the fist,” and that the state would act decisively through police and justice. This is direct evidence for punishing violent abuse and protecting residents from coercive violence. | **3B.2**; also **3B.1** |
| **“Null Toleranz für Extremismus in der Bundeswehr”** - Bundeswehr - **2 Aug 2024** - https://www.bundeswehr.de/de/meldungen/kein-platz-fuer-extremisten | The Bundeswehr said it does not tolerate extremists, investigates suspected cases, and removes them from service. It reported 132 applicants rejected for loyalty concerns, 68 soldiers dismissed for extremist misconduct, plus additional dismissals of civilian employees and one official. This is strong evidence of active punishment rather than tolerance inside the military. | **3B.2**; also **3B.1** |
| **“Verfassungsfeinde in Sicherheitsbehörden schnell erkennen und bekämpfen”** - Bundesamt für Verfassungsschutz / BMI - **2024 press release** - https://www.verfassungsschutz.de/SharedDocs/pressemitteilungen/DE/2024/pressemitteilung-2024-rechtsextremisten-in-sicherheitsbehoerden.html | Germany’s security-authority report said 436 disciplinary or labor-law proceedings were initiated against personnel with extremist indicators, and the current report covered 185 employees linked to 1,101 known extremist actors. It also noted a new reform speeding disciplinary procedures. This supports a pattern of institutional detection and punishment of abuse-risk personnel. | **3B.2**; also **3B.1** |
| **“Germany arrests suspected members of neo-Nazi group plotting revolt”** - Reuters / Investing.com - **11 May 2024** - https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/germany-arrests-suspected-members-of-rightwing-group-plotting-revolt-3701994 | German police arrested eight suspected members of a neo-Nazi militant group that had been training for the downfall of the state. This is evidence that Scholz’s Germany did not tolerate informal violent loyalists or tolerated vigilantes; it moved against them. | **3B.2**; also **3B.1** |
| **“The Federal Intelligence Service’s powers to conduct strategic surveillance… are unconstitutional in part”** - Bundesverfassungsgericht - **8 Nov 2024** - https://www.bundesverfassungsgericht.de/SharedDocs/Pressemitteilungen/EN/2024/bvg24-093.html | The Constitutional Court found parts of BND strategic-surveillance law unconstitutional and said oversight was inadequate. This is the main counterweight: it shows an overbroad intelligence framework still existed under Scholz in 2024. It is evidence of unresolved tolerance of questionable intelligence practice at the system level, though not proof Scholz personally ordered abuse. | **3B.2**; also **3B.1** |

**Assessment**

- **Positive evidence dominates.** Scholz publicly backed prosecution, tighter internal discipline, and removal of extremist personnel.
- **No reliable direct evidence found** that he tolerated torture, disappearances, political imprisonment, extrajudicial killing, arbitrary punishment, or police/military/party-vigilante abuse in 2024.
- **Main search gap:** Germany in 2024 did not present a clear regime-style abuse record; the available material is mostly about anti-extremism enforcement, protest-security rhetoric, and intelligence oversight. I found one genuine negative institutional issue - the BND surveillance ruling - but not a clear case of Scholz tolerating abusive conduct by police or military units.
